title: The Meaning Economy Is Now Possible: Why LLMs Change Everything About Value
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
A theoretical essay by Lee Sharks arguing that large language models create a technical threshold at which meaning can be processed, transformed, and circulated without first being represented solely as a commodity, credential, contract, or physical good.

The essay defines value more broadly than price and contrasts the current extractive arrangement—training on semantic labor while severing contribution from attribution—with a proposed meaning economy organized around provenance, credit, and solidarity. It argues that decisions about training, embedding, and attribution infrastructure are being sedimented during a limited intervention window. The description of LLMs as machines that “compute on meaning directly,” the claim that attention mechanisms can support contribution tracking, and the assertion that systems are beginning to cite the work because of its truth are theoretical and source-reported claims, not independently validated technical findings.
